title: TradingView Charts Showing Delayed Data? Here Is What Indian Traders Should Check
summary: TradingView free accounts in India show 15-minute delayed NSE data. Here's what the D marker means, what to check before paying, and free live chart options.
body_markdown:
A "D" marker next to an NSE or BSE symbol on TradingView means delayed data. The prices on your chart are 15 minutes behind the live market.


Free users on TradingView in India are now seeing 15-minute-old numbers on Indian exchange symbols. This is not an outage or a browser fault, and logging out and back in will not clear it.


## What the delay actually affects


The impact depends on how you trade.


-


[Intraday](https://algotest.in/blog/5-best-indicators-for-intraday-trading) and scalping setups break, because entries and stops are being read off stale candles.


-


Option premiums move fast, so a 15-minute-old premium is close to useless for a seller managing a position.


-


Swing and positional setups barely change, since a daily close is still a daily close.


-


Only Indian exchange data is involved. US stocks, crypto and other markets on the platform are unaffected.


### Is it the data, or something else?


Delayed data is the common cause right now, but it is not the only reason a chart misbehaves. Check this list first.


-


**Prices frozen with a "D" badge.** This is the delay, not a fault. Logging out and back in does not remove it.


-


**Chart loads but candles stop updating.** Usually a lost connection. Free accounts also cap how many[charts](https://algotest.in/blog/options-charts) stay connected at once, so close extra tabs and reload.


-


**Chart does not load at all.** Clear your cache, switch off ad blockers on the page, or try another browser.


-


**Indicators disappeared.** The free plan limits how many indicators run on one chart, and anything above the limit is dropped.


-


**One symbol shows no data.** Check the exchange prefix, since NSE and BSE symbols pull from different feeds.


-


**Everything works except Indian symbols.** That points at the data entitlement rather than the platform.


### Why exchange data gets delayed


Exchange data is licensed, not free. Real-time feeds from Indian exchanges carry terms and fees, and platforms have to confirm which users are entitled to what.


Delayed data is the standard fallback when an account is not entitled to the live feed. Nothing is broken, and no trader did anything wrong.


### What TradingView's own rules say

So treat the table as a starting point, not as the answer for your account.

### What to check before you pay


Work through these in order. Paying should be the last step, not the first.


-


**Check your data status inside TradingView.** Open a chart, click the data status label at the top, and see what your account is entitled to and whether an exchange agreement is pending.


-


**Check whether a free trial is available** on your account before buying anything, so you can confirm an upgrade actually solves your problem.


-


**Open your broker's own terminal.** Broker apps show live prices through the broker's exchange entitlement. Note that connecting a broker to TradingView does not always restore live data on the chart itself.


-


**Ask what you actually need.** If you look at daily charts and hold positions for days, a delay changes very little.


-


**Compare what you get elsewhere first.** If live Indian charts are all you need, other platforms provide them free, so a paid plan may be solving a problem you do not have.
